verdict.rationale: Mercury's documented REST API lets developers view and manage accounting-relevant data. It can list and get transactions, update transaction metadata and upload attachments, create, edit and delete categories, download statement PDFs, and list merchants and treasury statements [mercury-docs-12]. A dedicated Accounts Receivable API covers customers and invoices [mercury-docs-13, mercury-docs-45], with scoped read-write tokens, a sandbox, and write actions like categorizing transactions [mercury-docs-29, mercury-docs-35, mercury-docs-34]. Missing for 10: general-ledger, journal-entry or chart-of-accounts endpoints (accounting sync is via QuickBooks/Xero/NetSuite integrations rather than the API), and independent hands-on corroboration of the accounting endpoints.
